material_definitions: The samples are part of a series of solid solutions with the general formula Li(4-2x)MgxTi(5-x)/3O4.
The material is synthesized using a solid-state reaction method.
The structure of the samples is confirmed to be a spinel-type structure through X-ray diffraction.
Ionic conductivity was measured using AC impedance spectroscopy over a temperature range.

material_definitions: The Li1+xAlxTi2-x(PO4)3 system is a series of lithium-ion conducting solid electrolytes with a NASICON-type structure.
Materials were synthesized via solid-state reaction using Li2CO3, Al2O3, TiO2, and (NH4)2HPO4.
The ionic conductivity is optimized by substituting Ti4+ ions with Al3+ ions to increase the lithium-ion concentration.
The samples were typically sintered at temperatures around 1000 °C to improve grain boundary connectivity.

material_definitions: The ceramic electrolytes are based on the LiHf2(PO4)3 system.
The conductivity is enhanced by Li2O addition or by ion substitution in Li1+xMxHf2-x(PO4)3 (M = Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, or Y) systems.
The P21/n monoclinic phase transforms to the NASICON-type R3c rhombohedral phase above 1173 K.
The activation energy for Li+ ion migration decreases upon transitioning to the NASICON-type structure.
The activation energy for the bulk component of the NASICON-type structure was found to be 0.42 eV.
The materials belong to the LiHf2(PO4)3 + yLi2O system, where y ranges from 0 to 0.4, synthesized for use as solid lithium-ion conductors.
Li2O is added as a flux to promote densification, resulting in a glassy lithium phosphate phase at the grain boundaries during the sintering process.
Samples undergo a phase transition from a monoclinic P21/n phase to a rhombohedral NASICON-type R3c phase at elevated sintering temperatures.
The total ionic conductivity is influenced by both the densification and the formation of the NASICON-type crystal structure.
Li2O addition specifically lowers the activation energy at the grain boundaries, which significantly enhances the total conductivity.
